name: Smith machine Romanian deadlift
description: Set the stops below your intended range and start with the guided bar at upper-thigh height. Stand so the bar stays close to your legs through the machine path. Unrack with an overhand grip, soften your knees and brace. Push your hips back while keeping that knee bend nearly constant; lower only while your back stays stable. Drive your hips forward to stand, without leaning back. Re-rack securely before stepping away.

name: Standing cable hip abduction
description: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and fasten it securely around the ankle farther from the stack. Stand side-on, hold a stable support and set a light resistance. Brace with a soft bend in the supporting knee. Move the cuffed leg outward without turning your pelvis or leaning sideways, then return slowly without letting the stack slam. Complete the set and repeat on the other side.

name: Seated back extension machine
description: Select a light resistance and adjust the seat, feet and back pad according to the machine placard. Set the starting angle within a comfortable range and hold the handles. Brace your abdomen, keep your pelvis supported and extend your torso against the pad in a smooth motion. Stop at a comfortable upright position instead of arching back. Return slowly to the start without bouncing or letting the stack fall.

name: Rotary torso machine
description: Use a light stack setting. Adjust the seat or kneeling support and pads as shown on the machine placard, then choose a comfortable starting angle. Keep your supported body segment stable and hold the handles without pulling with your arms. Rotate the moving torso or lower-body assembly slowly through the intended range; avoid forcing the end position. Return under control, reset the starting angle for the other direction and repeat.

description: Choose enough assistance to keep the movement controlled. Hold the underhand chin-up handles, step onto the platform and position your knees or feet as the machine requires. Brace and pull your elbows down until your chin reaches handle height without swinging. Lower smoothly to a comfortable extended-arm position. Keep control of the moving platform as you step off.

name: Fan bike cardio
description: Adjust the seat so your knees remain slightly bent at the farthest pedal position and you can reach the moving handles without rounding your back. Start pedalling gently, then add a smooth push-pull of the arms. Keep your feet secure and coordinate both sides without jerking the handles. Maintain the effort you can control, then ease down gradually before the pedals stop and you dismount.

description: Adjust the seat or approved wheelchair platform, crank height and reach for your setup. Lock the seat and any required stabilizers; choose a comfortable handle radius. Slow down before stopping and use the machine supports when leaving.

Reduce your pace gradually and stop the pedals before getting off.

name: Machine pullover
description: Adjust the seat and starting position so your upper arms or elbows meet the work pads comfortably. Secure the provided restraint and position yourself using the machine entry lever if fitted. Brace against the support and drive your upper arms down through a comfortable arc, keeping your elbow angle nearly fixed. Return slowly without letting the load pull your shoulders into a forced stretch. Release the resistance using the entry mechanism before leaving.

name: V-squat machine
description: Set the platform and safety stop for the traditional orientation supported by your machine. Place your back against the back pad, position your shoulders under the pads and put both feet securely on the platform. Brace, extend your legs enough to release the latch, then lower by bending your knees and hips through a stable range. Push evenly to stand without snapping your knees straight. Re-engage the safety latch before leaving.

name: Tibialis raise machine
description: Sit with your working heel supported and the forefoot beneath the upper foot pad as shown on the machine. Start with light resistance and keep your knee and leg stable. Lift the forefoot toward your shin while your heel stays supported; pause briefly and lower slowly to the starting position. Use a comfortable ankle range without swinging the leg. Complete the set before changing sides or stepping clear.

name: Grip squeeze machine
description: Sit or position yourself at the gripper with a secure hold on its fixed and moving handles. Choose light resistance and keep your wrists in a comfortable neutral position. Close the moving handle with your fingers, keeping your forearms steady. Pause briefly, then let the handle open slowly without releasing your grip abruptly. Finish with the load safely resting before removing your hands.

name: Neck flexion machine
description: Use the lowest suitable resistance and get the machine setup checked before beginning. Adjust the seat and rotating head pad so the pad contacts the forehead; hold the handles and keep your trunk supported. Slowly nod forward slightly against the pad through a small comfortable range. Return under control without twisting, jerking or forcing the end position. Keep your shoulders still. Stop if the movement causes pain, dizziness or radiating symptoms.
